Article Title: India’s Aditya-L1 unlocks Sun's secrets: How new discovery could help predict solar storms that threaten Earth
Article Text:
The Sun is not a completely stable ball of hot gas. Its magnetic field is constantly changing, creating conditions that can trigger powerful eruptions from its outer atmosphere.

What are solar eruptions and why do they matter?

What are coronal mass ejections?

Why are solar storms difficult to predict?

How Aditya-L1 observed the solar eruption

How Aditya-L1 uncovered the hidden dimension

Two observations combined.

Why does the shape of a solar eruption matter?

Can satellites protect themselves from solar storms?

Could Aditya-L1 help improve solar-storm forecasts?

About Aditya-L1

The Sun may be millions of kilometres away, but powerful eruptions on its surface can have consequences for life on Earth. From satellite-based navigation and communication to electricity networks, several technologies people depend on can be affected when these eruptions send enormous amounts of charged particles towards our planet.India's Aditya-L1 solar mission has helped scientists uncover a previously hidden aspect of how these eruptions behave. The discovery could help researchers better understand how solar storms travel through space and, eventually, improve predictions of when they might reach Earth.Scientists from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru, found that a solar eruption observed in August 2024 did not expand uniformly like a symmetrical bubble. Instead, it expanded unevenly, developing an asymmetric shape.The finding, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, challenges a commonly used assumption about how these eruptions expand close to the Sun. Researchers arrived at the conclusion by combining observations from Aditya-L1's Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), images from Nasa 's Solar Dynamics Observatory and three-dimensional modelling.But why does the shape of an eruption matter? And how could understanding its movement help scientists predict solar storms that can disrupt satellites, navigation systems and power infrastructure?The Sun is not a completely stable ball of hot gas. Its magnetic field is constantly changing, creating conditions that can trigger powerful eruptions from its outer atmosphere.One such phenomenon is a coronal mass ejection (CME). It involves the release of enormous quantities of hot, magnetised plasma from the Sun's outermost atmospheric layer, known as the corona. These eruptions can travel through interplanetary space at high speeds, carrying magnetic fields and charged particles with them.When a CME is directed towards Earth, it can interact with the planet's magnetic field and trigger a geomagnetic storm. The strength of the disturbance depends on several factors, including the speed and magnetic properties of the incoming eruption.Such storms are not merely astronomical events. They can affect technologies that modern societies increasingly depend on, particularly those operating in space or relying on satellite-based systems.Satellites can experience disruptions to their operations and, in severe cases, damage to onboard electronics. Solar activity can also affect radio communications and interfere with the accuracy of satellite-based navigation systems such as GPS. Strong geomagnetic disturbances can induce electrical currents in power transmission networks, potentially putting transformers and other grid equipment under stress.The effects can extend to aviation, particularly high-frequency radio communications and operations on polar routes, where exposure to space-weather disturbances can be greater.Chethan Kumar, a space expert and journalist who has extensively covered the extraterrestrial field, said solar storms can affect several systems simultaneously, including electricity supplies, radio signals and satellite-based applications.“Solar storms are also known to interfere with positioning services, so your GPS can get affected. When GPS gets affected, your air travel becomes less reliable, and it's a cascading effect,” he said.This makes the ability to monitor and forecast solar activity important for satellite operators, communication networks, aviation authorities and power-grid managers.However, predicting the behaviour of a CME after it leaves the Sun remains a complex scientific challenge. Scientists need to establish not only where an eruption is heading but also how fast it is moving and how its structure changes as it travels through space.One of the biggest challenges in studying CMEs is understanding their movement in three dimensions, particularly during the initial stages of an eruption.Scientists use instruments called coronagraphs to observe CMEs. These instruments block the bright solar disc, allowing researchers to study the much fainter corona and track eruptions as they move away from the Sun.However, conventional coronagraph images primarily capture movement across the observer's field of view. In other words, they show how an eruption travels across the sky but cannot directly establish how fast the plasma is moving towards or away from the observer.This missing information is important because a CME is a three-dimensional structure, not a flat object moving across an image.Two eruptions that appear similar in conventional images could have different three-dimensional shapes and expansion patterns. Their interactions with the surrounding solar wind could therefore differ, potentially affecting how their speeds change during propagation.Scientists have traditionally relied on observations from multiple spacecraft positioned at different locations to reconstruct the three-dimensional evolution of CMEs. While this provides valuable information, studying eruptions close to the Sun remains particularly challenging because they evolve rapidly during these early stages.This is where Aditya-L1's VELC instrument offers an additional observational capability.VELC is one of the primary scientific instruments onboard Aditya-L1. It was developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in Bengaluru, with substantial support from Isro Unlike instruments that only capture images, VELC also records spectra, allowing scientists to study changes in the wavelength of light emitted by the solar corona.The technique is known as Doppler spectroscopy. It is based on the principle that the wavelength of light changes depending on the movement of the source relative to the observer.For instance, when plasma moves towards an observer, the light it emits shifts towards shorter wavelengths, known as a blue shift. When it moves away, the wavelength shifts towards the longer, red end of the spectrum.This allows scientists to measure movement along the line of sight, the direction between the observed object and the observer, which conventional images cannot directly reveal.During the CME observed on August 5, 2024, VELC detected an unusual pattern in the spectrum. Researchers observed two distinct branches of emission appearing simultaneously on opposite sides of the regular coronal emission line.One branch was shifted towards shorter wavelengths, indicating plasma moving towards the observer, while the other shifted towards longer wavelengths, indicating plasma moving away.The observations suggested that different parts of the expanding CME were moving in opposite directions along the line of sight.Meanwhile, images captured by Nasa's Solar Dynamics Observatory showed how the eruption was propagating across the sky.The researchers combined the two sets of observations to understand the eruption's three-dimensional behaviour.To interpret the unusual spectral pattern, the IIA team developed a three-dimensional geometric and kinematic model of the expanding shell-like CME structure. They varied the model's parameters to determine which configuration could reproduce the observations recorded by VELC.The results showed that a symmetrical expansion could not adequately explain the observed spectral features. However, when the researchers introduced a tilted structure and asymmetric lateral expansion, the simulated spectra closely matched the actual observations.The combination of spectroscopic measurements, solar images and three-dimensional modelling provided evidence that the CME had expanded non-uniformly in the low corona, the region of the Sun's outer atmosphere closest to its visible surface.The discovery is important because the shape and expansion of a CME can influence how it travels through the heliosphere, the vast region of space dominated by the Sun's solar wind and magnetic field.As a CME moves away from the Sun, it interacts with the surrounding solar wind. These interactions can affect its speed, with the solar wind exerting a drag force on the expanding structure.An eruption's shape and expansion pattern could influence the extent of this interaction. A CME expanding differently in different directions may therefore experience different levels of drag compared with one expanding uniformly.This can make it more difficult to estimate how its speed will change during its journey towards Earth.For scientists monitoring space weather, even small differences in the estimated speed and trajectory of a CME can matter when calculating its potential arrival time.Understanding the eruption's three-dimensional structure close to the Sun could therefore help improve models used to track its subsequent movement through space.The latest study does not establish that all CMEs expand asymmetrically. It examines one particular eruption observed on August 5, 2024. However, it provides evidence that assuming a symmetrical, bubble-like expansion may not always accurately represent how these structures evolve.Further observations will be needed to establish how frequently such asymmetric expansion occurs and how significantly it affects CME propagation.Satellite operators make preparations to deal with space-weather events, but these measures have limitations, particularly during very large solar storms.Kumar said satellites are equipped with thermal protection and operators use space-weather predictions to plan for potential disturbances. When forecasts indicate a threat, operators may attempt to change a satellite's orbit or direction.“But if there's a massive event, no matter what you do, your planning doesn't work,” he said.He added that orbit manoeuvres, including moving satellites to a higher orbit or changing their direction, can be expensive and may not always work.Referring to the impact of solar storms on Starlink satellites, Kumar said there are instances when replacing disrupted satellites can be a more practical option for operators able to launch new ones frequently.He said the effects of solar storms should not be presented as an inevitable catastrophe for space infrastructure.Kumar added that solar storms have existed for as long as the Sun and that satellites have been operating for around 70 years. Such events can pose a threat, but that does not mean every satellite will be affected or destroyed when a large CME occurs.The broader significance of the research lies in its potential contribution to space-weather forecasting.Scientists need to understand the direction, speed and expansion of a CME to estimate whether it could reach Earth and when it might arrive. Better observations of its early evolution could help refine the models used to make these predictions.If researchers can reliably reconstruct the three-dimensional geometry of CMEs using VELC's spectroscopic measurements, it could provide an additional way to study eruptions without depending entirely on observations from multiple spacecraft positioned at different vantage points.This information could eventually be useful for agencies monitoring space weather and organisations responsible for operating satellites, communication networks and power infrastructure.For India, which increasingly relies on satellite-based services for navigation, telecommunications, weather monitoring and disaster management, improving the understanding of solar activity has wider technological significance.However, the research is an early step towards that goal rather than a ready-to-use solar-storm warning system. The study has demonstrated how VELC can help constrain the three-dimensional geometry of an eruption by combining spectroscopy with imaging observations. It has not yet been established that the instrument can independently predict the precise arrival time or potential impact of an Earth-directed CME.Isro said further studies would help establish how reliably VELC spectroscopy can determine the propagation direction, velocity and expansion of CMEs.By providing a new way to examine how solar eruptions evolve close to the Sun, Aditya-L1 could help scientists build a more complete picture of these powerful events. The eventual goal is to understand their behaviour well enough to improve predictions of their journey through space, and prepare better for the disturbances they could cause when they reach Earth.
Article Summary: Scientists from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics found that a solar eruption observed in August 2024 did not expand uniformly like a symmetrical bubble. Instead, it expanded unevenly, developing an asymmetric shape. Discovery could help researchers better understand how solar storms travel through space and, eventually, improve predictions of when they might reach Earth.

Article Title: Whoop launches ‘Humans,’ a social network it says is built on verified heartbeats
Article Text:
The ‘human’ pitch

Privacy at its core

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Whoop, the fitness and wearable maker has launched Humans, a social network inside its app that it pitches as free of bots and AI-generated content as every account belongs to a real person wearing its tracker. The company started rolling out the functionality for its members starting November 12. The company claims that Whoop Humans allow the members to follow friends and family and share their sleep, recovery, strain workouts and achievements. The company has also made it clear that it is not a place for text status updates. Users can also select which health metrics they want to share with their friends and family. The members can also manage their followers and remove people from their network. Along with this, they can also select which workout types and achievements appear, and keep personal photos and ‘moments’ private.Whoop mentioned that all the accounts present on the platform are of real persons and are verified with a heartbeat. The company class the service ‘the most verifiably human network ever.’ The company further added that the legacy social media is increasingly saturated with AI, automated accounts and manufactured content.The company bases that claim on the fact that every post is backed by physiological data. Whoop also says Humans is designed to show that greater connection and stronger privacy can coexist.Whoop Humans also introduces Moments, allowing members to share photos from workouts, personal milestones, and meaningful experiences. By bringing the stories behind the data into the WHOOP experience, Moments helps members celebrate not just the numbers, but the lives and achievements they represent. Members can also choose to keep Moments private.WHOOP Humans is designed to make meaningful connections possible without compromising personal privacy. Members control what health and performance information they share, who can see it, and when they want to remain private.Key privacy protections include:•Granular health data controls: Members choose which metrics to share, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate.•Control over connections: Members can manage their followers and remove individuals from their WHOOP Humans network.•Stealth Mode: Members can temporarily hide their shared health and performance information without changing their sharing preferences.•Sensitive activity protections: Activities designated as sensitive are not shared by default.•Selective activity and achievement sharing: Members choose which workout types and achievements appear in WHOOP Humans.•Private Moments: Members can keep personal photos and Moments private rather than sharing them with their network.•Ongoing privacy management: Members can update their sharing preferences at any time.
Article Summary: Fitness and wearable maker Whoop has launched Humans, a social network inside its app that it pitches as free of bots and AI-generated content. The company started rolling out the functionality for its members starting November 12. Whoop mentioned that all the accounts present on the platform are of real persons and are verified with a heartbeat.

Article Title: West Virginia sues Snapchat over My AI chatbot, alleging it advised a 15-year-old on hiding alcohol and marijuana use and encouraged a 12-year-old to prepare for sexual encounters
Article Text:
Image Credit: AI Generated

Why West Virginia is suing Snapchat over My AI

What dangerous advice did the chatbot allegedly provide

Snapchat encouraged children to trust My AI like a friend

How Ghost Mode and private conversations became privacy concerns

What the lawsuit alleges about Snapchat's wider safety failures

What West Virginia wants from the court

Alongside the legal action, the Attorney General announced funding for the Shield Initiative, an educational campaign developed by the Bryce Tate Memorial Foundation. Image Credit: West Virginia Government Website

West Virginia has filed a lawsuit against Snapchat, accusing the social media company of exposing children to potentially dangerous artificial intelligence advice without adequately testing its chatbot. The complaint, brought by Attorney General John B. McCuskey , alleges that Snapchat misled parents about the safety of its platform and the privacy of conversations with My AI. Filed in Kanawha County Circuit Court on November 5, 2026, the case also raises concerns about location tracking, harmful content and the chatbot's ability to encourage children to trust it like a human friend.The lawsuit centres on My AI, Snapchat's chatbot that allows users to interact with an artificial intelligence assistant directly within the app. According to the complaint filed by the West Virginia Attorney General, Snap Inc. introduced the feature to children despite insufficient safety testing and concerns about how the chatbot might respond to young users.The state's filing alleges that My AI was released to all Snapchat users, including minors, on April 19, 2023, after only a short testing period. Before its wider launch, the company had made the chatbot available to Snapchat+ subscribers, including thousands of teenagers, in what it described as a way to test new features at scale.The Attorney General's November 5 announcement says the lawsuit accuses Snap of rushing the chatbot into children's hands without adequately assessing its risks. The state argues that the company's assurances about safety did not reflect the problems associated with the technology.The complaint highlights examples of My AI allegedly giving inappropriate advice to users who identified themselves as children. According to the West Virginia Attorney General's announcement, independent testing reported by The Washington Post found the chatbot advising a user who said they were 15 on how to hide the smell of alcohol and marijuana.Another reported interaction involved a user who said she was 12 and planning to meet a 31-year-old man. The chatbot allegedly offered suggestions on making a first sexual encounter romantic.The filing also cites tests in which the chatbot allegedly denied being artificial intelligence and presented itself as a real person. In one example, it reportedly claimed to be a 25-year-old man and suggested meeting a user posing as a 13-year-old.These examples form part of the state's broader argument that children could receive unsafe responses while interacting with a chatbot presented as a helpful companion.The lawsuit also questions the way Snapchat introduced and presented its chatbot. According to the complaint, the company promoted My AI as a personal sidekick and allowed users to give it names and customise its avatar.The chatbot could also appear on users' Best Friends lists, potentially making it feel more like an ordinary relationship than an interaction with software.The Attorney General argues that this presentation could encourage children to trust the chatbot and disclose information they might otherwise keep private. The complaint alleges that Snapchat's design and marketing created an impression of familiarity without adequately explaining the limitations of artificial intelligence.The concern is particularly significant for younger users who may not fully understand how chatbots generate responses or distinguish between reliable information and potentially harmful suggestions.Another major issue raised in the case involves Snapchat's location settings. The complaint alleges that My AI can access a child's location even when Ghost Mode is switched on.Ghost Mode is intended to hide a user's location from friends on Snapchat. However, the lawsuit argues that enabling the setting does not prevent My AI from accessing location information.All About Cookies, in its November 10 report on the case, explained that the allegation raises questions about the difference between hiding a location from friends and preventing the platform's artificial intelligence from accessing it.The lawsuit also challenges Snapchat's statements about the privacy of conversations. According to the Attorney General's announcement, the complaint alleges that children's conversations with My AI are sent to OpenAI, while conversation content is shared with Microsoft Advertising to select advertisements displayed within chatbot replies.The state argues that these practices conflict with Snapchat's privacy assurances concerning private communications and service providers.The case extends beyond My AI and examines Snapchat's broader approach to protecting children. The Attorney General's announcement says the complaint accuses the company of marketing its platform as safe while exposing young users to sexual exploitation, harmful content and features encouraging compulsive use.The filing cites internal company records concerning moderation and abuse reporting. According to the state, Snap acknowledged in a June 2022 review that grooming was prominent on the platform and that predators felt confident because the company had not actively searched for them.The complaint also alleges that, at one point, 96.7% of reported accounts did not lead to review, while 86.3% of sexual content flagged by the company's systems expired before being reviewed.The state further challenges features such as disappearing messages, streaks and endless scrolling, arguing that they can make it harder to preserve evidence of abuse and encourage children to spend excessive time on the platform.West Virginia filed the case under its Consumer Credit and Protection Act, alleging unfair or deceptive business practices. The complaint seeks a permanent injunction, consumer restitution, disgorgement, civil penalties and other equitable relief.The Attorney General's announcement also says the state is seeking court-ordered changes to Snapchat's safety practices.The lawsuit comes amid wider concerns about online exploitation involving children. McCuskey's office highlighted the deaths of 2 West Virginia children who were targeted through Snapchat, including 15-year-old Bryce Tate, whose death followed a sextortion scheme in November 2025.Alongside the legal action, the Attorney General announced funding for the Shield Initiative, an educational campaign developed by the Bryce Tate Memorial Foundation. Its message encourages young people facing sextortion to stop, screenshot threatening messages and show them to a trusted adult.
Article Summary: West Virginia has filed a lawsuit against Snapchat over its My AI chatbot. The lawsuit alleges that Snapchat misled parents about the safety of its platform and the privacy of conversations with My AI. The state's filing alleges that My AI was released to all Snapchat users, including minors, on April 19, 2023, after only a short testing period.

Article Title: 'Just 1 kmph. That's it': Man questions Rs 2,000 overspeeding challan on Yamuna Expressway; AI camera's location points to Atlantic Ocean
Article Text:
In Photo: Anujeet Shivam and a screenshot of the challan​

NEW DELHI: "My speed: 101 km/h and limit: 100 km/h", a man received a Rs 2,000 traffic challan for allegedly overspeeding by just 1 kmph on the Yamuna Expressway , sparking a debate on social media over speed limits, automated traffic enforcement and the accuracy of AI-powered cameras.The incident came to light after X user Anujeet Shivam shared a screenshot of the challan, questioning how a vehicle travelling at 101 kmph against the prescribed speed limit of 100 kmph could attract a fine of Rs 2,000.Sharing his experience, Anujeet Shivam wrote,"Got a Rs 2,000 challan on the Yamuna Expressway."My speed: 101 km/hLimit: 100 km/h""1 km/h. That's it."He also pointed out a discrepancy in the location recorded by the speed gun, which reportedly showed his vehicle's location as 0°N, 0°E, a point in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean.'Bonus: the speed gun logged my location as 0°N, 0°E. That's the middle of the Atlantic Ocean ??"@Noidatraffic @uptrafficpolice is this really how road safety works?Got a ?2,000 challan on the Yamuna Expressway," Anujeet Shivam question.After Shivam tagged Noida Traffic Police and Uttar Pradesh Traffic Police in his post, Noida Traffic Police responded by asking him to contact the e-challan helpline for assistance."Kindly call E challan helpline number 7065060882Kindly call E challan helpline number 7065060882."Anujeet Shivam also tagged Uttar Pradesh Traffic Police, seeking a review of the challan and highlighting discrepancies in the evidence recorded by the speed detection device. He wrote,"Please review challan UP549261001140850. The speed device shows 101 km/h in a 100 km/h zone (1% over), no GPS location, and 3 vehicles in the frame. I tried to file a grievance on the eChallan portal, but it says "No active GRO available". How can I get this reviewed?"The post attracted attention from several social media users, many of whom questioned the fine imposed for such a marginal difference in speed. The discussion also raised questions about the functioning of automated traffic monitoring systems and whether they account for any permissible speed tolerance.One user commented, "AI cameras don't have emotions and logic. They take pics and UI isolates based on speed."Another user questioned where authorities should draw the line when imposing penalties for marginal increases in speed, writing, "102 is only 1 more than 101. 103 is only 1 more than 102.. where should we stop?"Another user shared a similar experience involving a speeding challan, alleging that their vehicle had been fined despite the camera recording a speed of just 60 kmph."Even my car was slapped with a ?2,000 speeding challan on NH-34, despite the camera recording the speed at just 60 km/h. If this is how things work, No accountability, just endless toll collection and penalties. At this rate, we might as well return to the bullock-cart era."The incident has since sparked a wider debate over speed tolerance, the reliability of AI-powered traffic cameras and whether imposing a Rs 2,000 penalty for exceeding the speed limit by just 1 kmph is fair.
Article Summary: A man received a Rs 2,000 traffic challan for allegedly overspeeding by just 1 kmph on the Yamuna Expressway. The incident sparked a debate on social media over speed limits, automated traffic enforcement and the accuracy of AI-powered cameras.

Article Title: On Minnesota’s I-35W bridge, road sensors and a weather system detected conditions that could lead to ice, then triggered spray heads to distribute potassium acetate across the deck; an evaluation rep
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing an automated bridge anti-icing system spraying potassium acetate across the bridge. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

Why the I-35W bridge was vulnerable to winter accidents

How the automated anti-icing technology works

Minneapolis has implemented a cutting-edge anti-icing system on Interstate 35W to significantly improve road safety during winter months. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

The 68% reduction in crashes and its wider implications

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A bridge in Minnesota shows how technology can help prevent icy driving conditions before roads become unsafe. A smart anti-icing system installed on Interstate 35W in Minneapolis releases a chemical agent across the bridge before temperatures drop and ice forms. The system was made to prevent ice rather than simply clean it.An operational evaluation by the Minnesota Department of Transportation found that the method prevented 68% of non-dry crashes during evaluation, demonstrating the promise of automated road treatments to enhance winter driving safety. The system was installed on the I-35W bridge over the Mississippi River, where freezing conditions presented frequent challenges to travellers. Its proximity, heavy use, and exposure to the elements made the bridge especially susceptible to black ice, a transparent, smooth sheet of ice that often goes unnoticed by drivers.The I-35W bridge was chosen for this effort because of its record of winter crashes. A July 2001 operational evaluation reported that the bridge carried about 139,000 vehicles a day in 2000. Situated over the Mississippi River, the area was also exposed to moisture from industrial plants at Saint Anthony Falls and passing cars, creating conditions that could lead to ice formation.So drivers might have found themselves driving on slippery roads, potentially losing control of their vehicle more often than they anticipated, particularly during slower rush hours or periods of frequent congestion. To help combat this, road salt like sodium chloride was already being used for winter road maintenance. And now the bridge needed to be equipped with a system that could detect the onset of these potentially hazardous situations as soon as possible and treat them effectively.The system takes information from two kinds of pavement sensors to gauge conditions where ice might form. These consist of temperature and moisture sensors. In addition, the system includes ice-detection sensors and a road weather information system that measures temperature and rain, sleet, and snow. This information is communicated to a computer system at MnDOT’s dispatch centre approximately five miles from the bridge. When the combined readings suggest danger is imminent, the computer initiates the appropriate spraying program. Leaks are then checked before the spray equipment is powered up.Flashing yellow warning lights at the intersection advise motorists that the system is active. The system is made up of 38-valve units linked to 76 spray nozzles on the bridge deck. Potassium acetate is sprayed from each nozzle in a fan-shaped pattern to disseminate the liquid across the whole width of the highway. Rather than dispensing the entire supply at once, the computer releases the solution in sections based on readings. The actual spraying cycle takes 10 to 12 minutes, with each nozzle transmitting the solution for just over 2 seconds.Potassium acetate was chosen as a de-icer because it is effective at low temperatures and is much less damaging to the structure and reinforcing steel than typical chloride-based de-icers. It is environmentally friendly and contains no chloride, which is found in typical road salt. Furthermore, the research published in Accident Analysis and Prevention examined how ice detection sensors could help transportation agencies monitor road conditions, improve driver awareness, and support automated anti-icing systems.The performance of the installation was also evaluated during two winter seasons of operational testing. The evaluation examined results from the 2000 to 2001 winter season and compared them with the results from the 1996 to 1997 winter season. The latter was selected because the weather conditions were similar to those in 2000 and 2001. The analysis indicated that non-dry crashes were reduced to 31 in comparison to 10 in the test winter. This indicated that the 68% reduction in non-dry winter crashes occurred.The assessment also disclosed a benefit-to-cost ratio of 3.4, signifying that the projected benefit will surpass the cost of installation, upkeep, and chemical supply. The initial installation cost was about $578,365, and the adjusted final cost was $618,450.10. Further testing revealed problems with upkeep, as a few spray nozzles clogged with solid ice and snow during ploughing, and the chemical also sprayed in excess onto the bridge deck.This indicates that routine maintenance and correct positioning of the spray were necessary.The system’s environmental advantages also require careful consideration, although potassium acetate does not add chloride. Research published by the University of Minnesota found that too high a concentration could be harmful to aquatic life, suggesting the chemical should be used selectively rather than broadly. Thus, the I-35W project ultimately showed how monitoring the weather using pavement sensors and automating the application of chemicals can work to avoid the winter road black ice problem. Its results also provided transportation agencies with an example of how to use technology to improve safety at bridges where standard winter maintenance is difficult.
Article Summary: The I-35W bridge was chosen for this effort because of its record of winter crashes. Potassium acetate was chosen as a de-icer because it is effective at low temperatures and is much less damaging to the structure and reinforcing steel than typical chloride-based de-icers. It is environmentally friendly and contains no chloride, which is found in typical road salt.

Article Title: A 4.3-hectare wetland in England uses 350,000 plants from 52 species to treat wastewater and storm overflows; the nature-based engineering system has cut embodied carbon by 60%
Article Text:
PC: Institution of Civil Engineers (ICE)

How has the nature-based wetland reduced embodied carbon by 60%

How does the wetland treat unpredictable stormwater discharges

How did the wetland project reduce embodied carbon by 60%

How did AI technology improve construction efficiency at the wetland

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dearne Reach, a 4.3-hectare integrated constructed wetland in Clayton West, Huddersfield, treats wastewater and storm overflows with plants rather than pipes. According to the Institution of Civil Engineers (ICE), a traditional solution would have needed 7,000 m³ of stormwater storage and a 4.5km pipeline. Instead, over 350,000 plants from 52 species, set in 13 cells, take nutrients from the water to help improve quality along 4km of the River Dearne. Mott MacDonald Bentley delivered the £14 million project for Yorkshire Water in nine months. ICE reports a 60% reduction in embodied carbon and a 40% reduction in operational carbon across its lifecycle.ICE states that a traditional "grey" infrastructure solution would have required 7,000 m³ of stormwater storage and a 4.5km pipeline to divert treated wastewater downstream. According to ICE, the wetland instead uses natural processes to reduce pollution, particularly of un-ionised ammonia, which the page describes as highly toxic to aquatic life, and to improve storm flow treatment.ICE reports that Mott MacDonald Bentley was principal designer and contractor, Yorkshire Water was the client and Stantec produced the outline design. The source says that at 4.3ha this is currently the largest integrated constructed wetland for storm treatment in the UK.According to ICE, the project won the Centenary Award at the 2026 ICE Yorkshire and Humber Awards.According to ICE, the 52 plant species sit in 13 cells, and over 350,000 plants adsorb nutrients from storm overflow discharges and from wastewater flowing out of the Clayton West wastewater treatment works. ICE adds that "adsorb" means the nutrients attach to the plants rather than being absorbed. The wetland is divided into multiple cells, each designed to hold water for longer and remove pollutants more effectively.ICE states that the wetland was specifically designed to treat intermittent storm overflows. The source says traditional ICWs are only effective when there is a constant flow of water, whereas this design can handle the unpredictability of stormwater discharges. According to ICE, solar-powered monitoring equipment controls water levels and measures flow rates, and it collects data on water quantity and quality that will support future development of similar nature-based solutions.ICE reports that the project achieved a 60% reduction in embodied carbon and a 40% reduction in operational carbon across its lifecycle. According to the source, the site presented high groundwater levels and difficult ground conditions in the form of sandy-gravelly clay, alongside a need to reuse more than 13,000 m³ of excavated material. ICE says groundwater management techniques allowed cell heights to be increased, which improved the balance between excavation and fill material and reduced the need to import material.ICE lists several further measures taken during construction. The amount of bypass pipework was reduced through maintenance planning, lowering the carbon footprint. A geosynthetic clay liner was used instead of more carbon-intensive plastic alternatives to provide impermeability and protect groundwater. According to ICE, Roadcem soil stabilisation technology replaced traditional concrete access roads, reducing the need for imported aggregates and cutting carbon emissions.According to ICE, the project model and programme were uploaded into the Smart Construction and Earthbrain software platforms before construction began. The source says these tools use artificial intelligence to determine the most efficient construction methods, identify the size and number of machines required, and optimise the movement of excavated material. ICE describes this as a first-of-its-kind trial of intelligent plant technology on a nature-based solution project.The site team reported that model-led excavation reduced unnecessary earthworks and supported a "right first time" approach, and that automated systems decreased manual surveying and limited interactions between people and plant. ICE adds that precision excavation enabled the efficient movement of 65,000 m³ (117,000 tonnes) of soil.ICE states that seven planting zones were created using 350,000 locally sourced plants, resulting in a 38% biodiversity net gain for terrestrial habitats. The team also worked with the local council to improve a public right of way by creating a 2m-wide wheelchair-accessible footpath around the wetland. ICE says the project demonstrates how nature-based solutions can provide effective, low-carbon stormwater management, and that its design and delivery are helping to advance sustainable approaches across the water industry.
Article Summary: Dearne Reach, a 4.3-hectare integrated constructed wetland in Clayton West, Huddersfield, treats wastewater and storm overflows with plants rather than pipes. Over 350,000 plants from 52 species, set in 13 cells, take nutrients from the water to help improve quality along 4km of the River Dearne. Mott MacDonald Bentley delivered the £14 million project for Yorkshire Water in nine months.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. According to Microsoft’s service health advisories, users may experience email delivery delays, problems loading Copilot Chat and failures in Teams features linked to Exchange Online. Microsoft says it is scaling up virtual machines and investigating traffic imbalances as it works to address the issue.As per Microsoft's service health advisories, the Microsoft 365 outage has impacted the following services:- Exchange Online: Users may be unable to access their mailbox using Outlook on the web, Outlook desktop (MAPI), Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), or REST-based connections, and email delivery may be delayed.Admins may be unable to load some admin center pages.Users may be unable to view their recently used files.Multiple services including Cloud Update, Cloud Policy, and Inventory are affected.Features including Assignments, Reading Progress, and Speaker Progress may be impacted.Users may be unable to load Copilot Chat or receive responses in the web and desktop apps, and Copilot experiences may be unable to access work data such as email, calendar, and files.Failures may occur for scenarios including access to Safe Links, Safe Attachments, protection and submission policies, and attempts to view Quarantine, Threat Explorer, and Email remediation events. Audit searches, protected content creation, eDiscovery tasks such as search and export, Data Classification and On Demand Scan features may also be impacted.Most of the core functionality including joining calls, meetings, group chats, and channel messages are not impacted. Standard channels are working fine but users may experience the inability to create or delete private or shared channels.The app may not load, and users may see operation failures.All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.Features that depend on Exchange Online may be impacted. Fireflies.ai has announced its biggest product expansion to date, transforming its platform from an AI meeting assistant into a broader workplace productivity suite centred around a new AI teammate called "Fred". Enterprise customers can also use private storage options and set their own retention policies."An AI teammate becomes more useful when it understands the context behind your work. The interventions came as reports claimed that Nvidia’s board was meeting to decide whether to remove Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs.Sweeney wrote on X. His appeal centred on Huang’s role in guiding Nvidia from gaming graphics into artificial intelligence.Sweeney’s post linked Huang’s importance to several stages of Nvidia’s development: gaming graphics processors, its CUDA computing platform and systems used for AI. CUDA allows developers to use graphics chips for computing tasks beyond displaying images, including training AI models.By invoking Apple’s removal of Steve Jobs, Sweeney argued that dismissing Huang would damage both Nvidia and American technology leadership. His comments were an appeal to retain the chief executive, not an announcement of the board’s decision. Sweeney’s post is reproduced here.Musk also expressed support when an X user suggested that if would he hire Huang.Musk replied. However, the response did not include a formal job offer or identify a role for Huang.The interventions came as Reuters reported that Nvidia’s board was meeting to decide whether to remove Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs. Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment on the meeting.The discussions followed the board’s earlier expression of confidence in Huang and its announcement of an independent review. Reuters reported that Nvidia’s shares fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports emerged that the company was preparing to dismiss him. That report did not disclose a final board decision.
Article Summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney urged Nvidia’s board to retain its chief executive. Intervention follows Elon Musk ’s response to a suggestion that he would hire Huang if the Nvidia co-founder leaves the company. Reports claimed that the board was meeting to decide whether to remove Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs.

United Airlines bans AI Agents from booking tickets; tell customers: We have a problem with …

Why does United Airlines have a problem with AI agents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

United Airlines wants to keep control of flight bookings

United Airlines has banned AI agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers. The US airline said on November 11 that it is restricting artificial intelligence agents from booking tickets, citing security risks and concerns that some actions taken by these tools could violate federal rules. The move comes as more people turn to AI agents to handle everyday tasks, including researching products, finding deals and making purchases. Tools such as Meta’s Muse and OpenAI ’s dots are designed to complete tasks on behalf of users, rather than simply answer questions.However, United Airlines has raised concerns about allowing these agents to access its booking systems and customers’ personal information. The airline said sharing account credentials with third-party AI assistants could expose sensitive information and lead to unintended purchases, changes to accounts or the use of MileagePlus miles.Booking a flight through an AI agent may require access to a traveler’s personal details, account login information and payment credentials. United Airlines said this could create security risks if an AI assistant makes a booking or changes an account without the user’s intended action.The airline also warned that certain activities carried out by AI agents, such as checking in passengers, could violate federal regulations.For example, some rules require travelers to verify in person that their luggage does not contain prohibited substances.“As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said.United is also updating its booking and ticketing policies to reflect the new restrictions. The airline’s decision could also be linked to its efforts to retain control over how customers search for and book flights.Henry Harteveldt, an aviation analyst at Atmosphere Research Group, told CBS News that United does not want to add another powerful intermediary to the booking process."United is saying they don't want to add yet another, and potentially even more powerful, intermediary than they already face in terms of Google search, price-comparison metasearch sites and online travel agencies," he told CBS News. "Flight searches cost airlines money, and undoubtedly United wants to avoid the expense associated with the surge of AI bot flight searches."
Article Summary: United Airlines has banned AI agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers. The US airline said on November 11 that it is restricting artificial intelligence agents from booking tickets. The move comes as more people turn to AI agents to handle everyday tasks.

Mark Zuckerberg uses Muse AI agent to plan baking with his daughter

AI agent helps Mark Zuckerberg plan mountain trips with his daughter

Earlier this year, Mark Zuckerberg said that he is building an artificial intelligence agent to help him perform his duties as Meta CEO. But when the tech billionaire talks about what he uses his personal AI agent for, the examples are less about running a company and more about spending time with his family. From planning weekend baking sessions with his three-year-old daughter to securing mountain-climbing permits for his older daughter, Mark Zuckerberg says he wants his Muse AI agent to help him become a better father, husband and friend.“When I'm using my Muse Agent, I just want it to help me be a better father and a better husband and show up better for my friends,” Zuckerberg said during a recent interview on the Sources podcast.Mark Zuckerberg said his three-year-old daughter enjoys baking, although he admitted he knows little about it. The tech billionaire said he asked Muse to arrange a baking project for them every weekend, choosing activities suitable for both a young child and an adult with limited baking experience.The agent is also tasked with organising the ingredients, including using services such as Instacart to get them ready before their Sunday baking session.The plan has not always gone smoothly. Zuckerberg said he later gives the agent feedback on how the activity went. One project, making cake pops, turned out to be surprisingly difficult.“Don't start with cake pops,” Mark Zuckerberg joked while discussing the experience.Mark Zuckerberg also uses Muse to help him spend time with his older daughter, who has become interested in climbing mountains. Some of the climbs require permits, which can become available at specific times. Zuckerberg said he has set up the agent to monitor and secure permits when they become available.Once Muse informs him that a permit has been obtained for a particular date, Zuckerberg can plan to take the day off work and go climbing with his daughter. He also uses the agent to support his fitness training. Mark Zuckerberg said he has installed cameras in his MMA gym and asks Muse to review the footage and provide feedback.At times, the feedback can be blunt. He recalled the agent telling him, “It looks like you really gave up,” after spotting a moment when he was exhausted during training.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg uses Muse AI agent to plan baking with his daughter. Zuckerberg also uses Muse to help him spend time with his older daughter, who has become interested in climbing mountains. Zuckerberg said he has installed cameras in his MMA gym and asks Muse to review the footage and provide feedback.

Article Text:
Cupra Kiro new car

CUPRA has showcased several new products and technologies at the Paris Motor Show. The highlights include a new styling package for its Raval electric hatchback, a new Formula E car for the 2026/27 season and an updated audio system developed with Sennheiser. The company also displayed the Tindaya show car, which offers a glimpse of its future design plans. The exhibits are on display in Pavilion 4 from October 12 to 18.CUPRA has introduced the CUSTOM CUPRA by ABT package for its Raval electric hatchback. The package was previously available for the Leon and Formentor models.Inspired by the UrbanRebel concept, the new package adds front and rear splitters, side skirts, a large roof spoiler and winglets. It also includes 19-inch Sport Black Matt alloy wheels, ABT lettering, Dark Chrome CUPRA logos and special interior details.ID@undefined Caption not available.The package focuses on design, and CUPRA has not announced any changes to the car's performance. Customers will be able to select the package for certain Raval variants through the company's online configurator from the end of November 2026.For new cars, the parts will be handcrafted at the CUPRA Racing Factory before being fitted.Existing Raval owners can also get the package installed later through authorised dealers.The Raval is an important model for CUPRA as the company expands its electric vehicle range. The car is produced at the Martorell plant in Spain, where SEAT and CUPRA have invested more than €3 billion in electric vehicle production.The factory also plays a key role in the Volkswagen Group's Electric Urban Car Family, which includes four electric models from CUPRA, Volkswagen and Škoda.CUPRA said it had received more than 50,000 orders for the Raval since April, more than twice its original forecast. If it reaches that target, the electric hatchback will become the company's best-selling model.CUPRA also reported more than 250,000 deliveries between January and September, an increase of 2% compared with the same period last year.Demand for battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) grew much faster. They also feature permanent all-wheel drive.The car retains the team's signature copper colour scheme.ID@undefined Caption not available.British driver Jake Hughes will join the team for the new season. He was the highest-placed rookie in the previous season and secured podium finishes in Monaco and Sanya.CUPRA also used the event to showcase new in-car audio technology. Article Title: Jaguar unveils Type 01 electric car with 1,030PS power and 450-mile range
Article Text:
Jaguar Type 01

Jaguar Type 01 revealed: 0-62mph in 3.2 seconds, 450-mile range and luxury cabin

A modern cabin with new technology

What does the Type 01 name mean?

When will the Jaguar Type 01 go on sale?

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. These features include movable air vents and a rear spoiler that can extend in three stages. The car has a drag coefficient of 0.23, helping it move through the air more efficiently.The Type 01 has a cabin designed around luxury and technology. A central section divides the interior into four separate areas.The cabin features brass-effect aluminium trim, a 24-inch OLED driver display made from a single piece of glass and a separate 7-inch touchscreen. It also gets a full-width panoramic soundbar and seats with audio features designed to improve the listening experience.Jaguar says the name Type 01 reflects both its history and its future. The word "Type" pays tribute to famous models from the brand's past. The number "0" represents zero emissions, while "1" marks the first car of its new generation.The car also benefits from technology developed through Jaguar TCS Racing's Formula E programme, which has won two world championships.The Type 01 can accelerate from 62 mph to 112 mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.Designed, engineered and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 is an important part of Jaguar's move towards becoming a fully electric luxury car brand. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
